text: Across 19 organisms and 14 metals (86 organism × metal pairs), 4,304 of 10,821 metal-important gene records (39.8%) were also important under NaCl stress.

text: The report interprets metal–NaCl gene overlap as general cellular vulnerability shared between metal and osmotic/ionic stress.
quote: This substantial overlap exists for every metal tested — from 9.2% for molybdenum to 57.6% for manganese — indicating that a large fraction of the "metal fitness" signal reflects general cellular vulnerability shared between metal and osmotic/ionic stress.
heading: 1. 39.8% of Metal-Important Genes Are Also NaCl-Important

text: Synechococcus elongatus (SynE) was a shared-stress outlier at 88.6% (565/638 genes), driven by 12 NaCl dose-response experiments spanning 0.5–250 mM, compared with 1–6 NaCl experiments for other organisms.

heading: 1. 39.8% of Metal-Important Genes Are Also NaCl-Important
